# Atmospheric & river forcing {.unnumbered}

*This chapter describes the surface and freshwater forcing, and introduces the
Pioneer River source that drives the flood scenario.*

The model is forced at the surface by gridded atmospheric fields and at the
river inflows by point sources.

::: {.callout-note}
The atmospheric (`sflux`) details and the full river inventory are still to be
documented here — see the planned content below.
:::

## River point sources

Freshwater enters through point sources defined by three coupled files:
`source_sink.in` lists the mesh elements that receive inflow, `vsource.th`
carries the flow time series (m³ s⁻¹) for each, and `msource.th` carries the
matching tracer concentrations. The dominant inflow is the **Pioneer River**
(source #3), discharged at the Bureau of Meteorology gauge 125013A near the
Dumbleton Pump Station.

The source enters in the shallow upper river, where the receiving cell is small
and intermittently dry — which is what drives the high injection ratio examined
in the [conservation testing](../part4-nutrient-budget/16-conservation-testing.qmd).
The map below shows the current source location together with candidate
relocation cells considered during that investigation.

![The Pioneer River source location and candidate cells, on the upper-river bathymetry. Source: `analytics/pioneer_region_flux/archive/src3_candidates_map.py`](../../assets/images/setup/src3_candidates_map.png){#fig-src-candidates}
